doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Cage in Louisiana, minstrels and learning fiddle
title: Pay for playing fife and fiddle
summary: Cage says he earned two or three dollars a night for playing, since nobody paid much.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I'd run off when I got ready. Were you playing any music then? Were you playing your fiddle? Playing any okay in five. They didn't pay you to do that I bet, huh? No, no sir. They didn't care if you never played. You didn't make a nickel? A penny?
No, I worked six months for $6.
No, I mean playing the five.
Oh, I'd get two, three dollars maybe. One dollar or something like that a night. They didn't pay nobody much.
Well, I guess you could buy quite a bit with a dollar out there. Oh, yes sir. In those times.
